flashcard_questions.q: What happens when two like magnetic poles are brought together?

flashcard_questions.a: A magnet that produces its own magnetic field all the time.
A magnetic material that becomes magnetised only while inside a magnetic field.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is steel used for permanent magnets rather than iron?
flashcard_questions.a: Steel keeps its magnetism when it is removed from a magnetic field.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does an electromagnet use an iron core?
flashcard_questions.a: Iron loses its magnetism almost immediately when the current is switched off.

flashcard_questions.q: In which direction do magnetic field lines run outside a magnet?
flashcard_questions.a: From the north pole to the south pole.

flashcard_questions.q: What shape is the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire?
flashcard_questions.a: Concentric circles centred on the wire.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a solenoid in electromagnetism?
flashcard_questions.a: A coil of wire that produces a magnetic field when current flows through it.

flashcard_questions.q: Name one way to increase the strength of an electromagnet.

flashcard_questions.a: The force felt by a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation gives the force on a conductor in a magnetic field?
What is the unit of magnetic flux density?
In Fleming's left-hand rule, what does the first finger show?
flashcard_questions.a: The direction of the magnetic field, from north to south.

flashcard_questions.q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, what does the thumb show?
flashcard_questions.a: The direction of motion, which is the force on the conductor.

flashcard_questions.q: What does a split-ring commutator do in a DC motor?
flashcard_questions.a: It reverses the current every half turn so the coil keeps spinning the same way.
